answer: LINE’s claim is that it can scale to very large graphs, whereas the BlogCatalog, PPI, and Wikipedia networks are comparatively small benchmark networks by size (especially in number of nodes and edges) and therefore do not by themselves demonstrate the same level of scalability challenge. The contrast is that LINE is designed for massive, real-world graphs, while those datasets are much smaller test cases. LINE’s edge-sampling algorithm helps bridge that gap by training on sampled edges rather than repeatedly processing the full graph, which reduces memory use and computation per update and makes optimization feasible on large networks.
